University of Rhode Island Faculty Senate RESOLUTION TO DEFEND ACADEMIC FREEDOM AND REJECT ANY ATTEMPT TO RATIONALE: WHEREAS state legislative proposals have been introduced and enacted across the United States targeting academic discussion of racism (including Critical Race Theory) and related issues in American history in schools, colleges, and universities.
WHEREAS these legislative proposals vary but all seek to prohibit or restrict curricula on what are labeled "divisive concepts” in the teaching and education of students.
WHEREAS the term“divisive”is indeterminate,subjective,and limits the capacity of cducators toexplore a wide variety of topics based on vague criteria incommensurate to the goals of education and the development of essential critical thinking skills. engaged and informed citizens.
WHEREAS the University of Rhode Island (URI) has a stated commitment to diversity, cquity, and inclusion (DEl), and to mitigating inequities related to diverse populations.

WHEREAS URI President Marc Parlange has appealed to “all Americans to face the truth about our work that still remains to be done to dismantle systemic racism inour communities andinstitutions,and then tocommit to bc ing part of bringing about that change." WHEREAS in view of the ongoing rcality of violence and discrimination perpetrated against the Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC) community, the URI has committed itself to a sincere reconsideration of policies and practices at URI that perpetuate racist patterns.
WHEREAS The American Association of University of Professor(AAUP)and URI's A A UP chapter affirm the importance of academic freedom to the proper functioning of universities, citing the American Association of University Professors1940 statement of Principles on Academic Freedom and Tenure.
WHEREAS the URI's University Manual 6.11.12 and its AAUP contract 7.2 maintain“Academic freedom is essential ... and applies to both teaching and research .. .
Academic freedom in its teaching aspects is fundamental for the protection of the rights of the teacher in teaching and of the student to freedom in learning.

WHEREAS approximately150 organizations,including the AAUPand the Association of American Colleges and Universities (AACU), issued the Joint Statcmcnt on Legislative Efforts to Restrict Education about Racism and American History (June 16, 2021) stating their“firm opposition to a spate of legislative proposals being introduced across the country that target academic lessons, presentations, and discussions of under principles of academic freedom that have been widely endorsed, professors are entitled to freedom in the classroom in discussing their subject.
Educators, not politicians, should make decisions about teaching and learning."

WHEREASin a nation that hasfor centuriesstruggledwith issues of racialinequity and injustice,many students donothave adequateknowledgeofBIPOCand LGBTQIAhistory and thepoliciesthatcontributed to inequities, the University of Rhode Island has a responsibility and opportunity to help build equity and social justice.
RESOLUTION THEREFOREBEITRESOLVEDthattheFacultySenaterejects any attemptsbybodiesoutsidethe University to restrict or dictate university curriculum on any matter, including matters related to racial and social justice, and will stand firm against encroachment on faculty authority by any organization.
BEITFURTHERRESOLVED that theFacultySenate standswithourK-12colleaguesatpublic and private schools throughout Rhode Island as well as across the country who may be affected by this restrictive legislation.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Faculty Senate calls upon the entire community of the University to affirm they reject any attempts by bodies external to the University of Rhode Island to restrict or dictate university curriculum on any matter, including matters related toracial and social justice, and will stand firm against encroachment on faculty authority and university sovereignty.
BEIT FURTHERREVOLVED that theUniversity standsbchinditsfaculty and theprinciple of academic freedom as articulated in the 1940 statement of Principles on Academic Freedom and Tenure.
BEITFURTHERRESOLVEDthat theFacultySenate affirms theJointStatementonEffortstoRestrict Education about Racism, authored by the AAUP, PEN America, the American Historical Association, and the Association of American Colleges and Universities, endorsed by over seventy organizations, and issued on June 16, 2021.
